source.diagram: Al2O3-CaO phase diagram after Nurse et al. [1, 2]
source.caption: Atlas text (printed p. 39): 'Fig. 3.19. Al2O3-CaO phase diagram after Nurse et al. [1, 2]. For similar versions of the system with incongruent melting of CaO·Al2O3 and CaO·2Al2O3, see also Imlach, Glasser [3] and Chatterjee, Zhmoidin [4]. In contrast, congruent melting of these compounds has been reported by Rankin, Wright [5], Rolin, Thanh [6], Rao [7] and accepted recently in the thermodynamic assessment of the system by Hallstedt [8]. The 12CaO·7Al2O3 phase reported previously by Nurse et al. [2] as stabilized by OH groups, has been definitely found by Jeevaratnam et al. [9], Imlach et al. [10], Cockayne, Lent [11] and Gladkiy at al. [12] to exist in the anhydrous state. According to Imlach et al. [10], the 12CaO·7Al2O3 phase is non-stoichiometric, with a small excess of oxygen, and the minimum oxygen partial pressure in the atmosphere leading to the formation of this phase is 10^-7.3 atm (Gladkiy at al. [12]). The melting point of the 12CaO·7Al2O3 phase, 1413 °C, has been taken from Cockayne, Lent [11]. The liquidus relations in the vicinity of 12CaO·7Al2O3, as well as the location of both eutectics, have been drawn schematically in conformity with the 3CaO·Al2O3- and CaO·Al2O3-liquidus determined by Nurse et al. [2]. For recent thermodynamic assessment of the system and calculated phase diagram, see also Eriksson, Pelton [13].' References: [1] R. W. Nurse, J. H. Welch, A. J. Majumdar: Trans. J. Br. Ceram. Soc. 64 (1965) No. 2, p. 409/18; [2] R. W. Nurse, J. H. Welch, A. J. Majumdar: Trans. J. Br. Ceram. Soc. 64 (1965) No. 6, p. 323/32; [3] J. A. Imlach, F. P. Glasser: Trans. J. Br. Ceram. Soc. 67 (1968) No. 12, p. 581/609; [4] A. K. Chatterjee, G. I. Zhmoidin: J. Mater. Sci. 7 (1972) No. 1, p. 93/7; [5] G. A. Rankin, F. E. Wright: Am. J. Sci., 4th Ser. 39 (1915), p. 1/79; [6] M. Rolin, P. H. Thanh: Rev. Int. Hautes Tempér. et Réfract. 2 (1965) No. 2, p. 175/85; [7] M. R. Rao: J. Am. Ceram. Soc. 51 (1968) No. 1, p. 50/4; [8] B. Hallstedt: J. Am. Ceram. Soc. 73 (1990) No. 1, p. 15/23; [9] J. Jeevaratnam, F. P. Glasser, L. S. D. Glasser: J. Am. Ceram. Soc. 47 (1964) No. 2, p. 105/6; [10] J. A. Imlach: Cem. Concr. Res. 1 (1971), p. 57/61; [11] B. Cockayne, B. Lent: J. Cryst. Growth 46 (1979), p. 467/73; [12] V. N. Gladkiy, I. S. Kulikov, L. V. Ostrovskaya, A. A. Telegin: Izv. Akad. Nauk SSSR, Metal. (1980), p. 63/7; [13] G. Eriksson, A. D. Pelton: Metall. Trans. B 24B (1993), p. 807/15.

invariantPoints.notes: Incongruent melting of 3CaO·Al2O3: lime + liquid → 3CaO·Al2O3. The junction carries the printed label '67.2', but it is drawn at ≈57 mass% CaO, on the Al2O3 side of the 3CaO·Al2O3 line (62.3 wt% stoichiometric), as the liquid of an incongruently melting C3A must be; 67.2 would lie on the lime side. The label is taken as a misprint and the drawn composition is used.
